World Tree
Tree of Life | nicknames = | type = Tree, planar pathway | location = [[Outer Planes]], [[Astral Plane]], [[Prime Material plane]] | basicrefs = {{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|45}}{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|6}}{{Cite dungeon/196/Backdrop: Moonshae Isles|12}} | useon = | origin = | value = | usage = | consumedby = | poisonousto = | lifespan = | genrefs = | height = {{SI|23|mi|k}} | trunkdiameter = {{SIrange|1200|4000|ft}} | leaftype = | leafcolor = Blue-black | flowercolor = | color = | stemcolor = | distinctions = | appearrefs = {{Cite dungeon/149/Enemies of My Enemy|63}}{{Cite book/Expedition to the Demonweb Pits|38-40}}{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Travelogue|42-43}} | first = | based = [[wikipedia:en:Yggdrasil|Yggdrasil]] (Norse) }} '''Yggdrasil''', also known as the '''World Ash''', was a cosmic plane-spanning tree that linked the [[Prime Material Plane]] through the [[Astral Plane]] to the [[Outer Planes]] that were important to the [[Norse pantheon]].{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|72}}{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|44}} {{quote |Down the tree is easy; back up is hard. |[[Tisk]] the [[ratatosk]] }} ==Description== Yggdrasil was a silver-barked [[ash]] tree. Its leaves were blue-black and oval shaped and its rough bark resembled flaking gray clay. It was made of a type of divine wood that was immune to [[fire]], although fallen branches and leaves could be safely used for cooking fires. Spiraling along the main trunk, planks and sets of steps were carved or mounted onto the tree to facilitate traffic. The tree was surrounded by sky in all directions. It produced seeds, but they were known to be sterile by the [[elf|elven]] inhabitants of [[Arborea]] and [[Alfheim]].{{Cite book/In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|51}} The entire tree was {{SI|23|mi|k|long=yes}} tall, with a {{SIAdj|15|mi|k|adj=wide}} canopy. Its trunk was {{SI|4000|ft|long=yes}} in diameter at the bottom, but tapered down to a diameter of {{SI|1200|ft|long=yes}} at the point where it started to branch. All branches of the tree resembled enormous trees themselves, extending for up to {{SI|10|mi|k|long=yes}}. Many, but not all of them ended in two-way ''[[portal]]s'', which resembled the [[color pool]]s of the Astral Plane. Since there were many dead ends along the tree's branches, traveling without a guide or directions often resulted in long detours.{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|42-43}} Climbing the tree was difficult, but it was possible to get better footing by wearing [[dagger boots|spiked boots]]. The trip was made more perilous by the fact that [[Gravity plane|gravity]] was not constant along the tree. Throughout most of the trajectory, it pointed towards the center of the tree's trunk, but it slowly changed to match its destination plane as one approached a ''portal''. It was usually possible to predict when gravity would change by observing the direction of the moss growth along the trunk. Day and night followed an erratic cycle around the tree. During the day, sunlight percolated through the leaves, but provided full illumination until, at sunset, the sun appeared to move beyond a foggy horizon. At night, the tree was illuminated by countless stars that hung from the branches themselves. It was possible to reach out for one of those stars by climbing to the end of a branch. If grabbed, the star functioned like an ''[[Ioun stone]]'', casting a continuous ''[[daylight]]'' spell around its wearer, and holding on to its magic for up to 30 days after being separated from the tree. However, unless the attempt was performed by or in the company of a [[dwarf]], a worshiper of the Norse pantheon, or a mortal with a [[chaotic good]] disposition, reaching out to a star immediately triggered the break of dawn and caused the star to disappear. It was not understood why the stars of Yggdrasil were always out of reach to some people. ==Cosmography== [[File:Yggdrasil2Hades.jpg|right|thumb|300px|''Yggdrasil's planar connections.'']] Yggdrasil was so massive that it could almost be considered a plane in its own right. It even had certain planar characteristics of its own, such as a mild affinity towards [[chaos]] and a mild enhancement of plant- and [[:Category:Chaotic spells|chaotic]]-related [[spells]]. The tree's roots were in [[Niflheim]] (the second layer of [[Hades]]), and its crown was in [[Ysgard (layer)|Ysgard]] (the homonymous first layer of [[Ysgard]]) as described by the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model. Other roots and branches penetrated the Prime planes where Norse [[deities]] were recognized, allowing travelers to climb the tree until they reached a portal very similar to a ''[[color pool]]'' and step through to their destination. The entry point into Niflheim was usually a favorite among travelers because it avoided the first layer of [[Oinos]], a frequent battleground of the [[Blood War]]. At the other end of Yggdrasil was the first layer of the plane of Ysgard, the home of the rest of the Norse pantheon. Ysgard contained many realms including [[Jotunheim]], [[Alfheim]], [[Vanaheim]], and the grand realm that gave the layer its name, [[Asgard]].{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|95}} The tree also extended its branches to the second layer, [[Muspelheim]].{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|138}} All of these divine domains were near (in a cosmic sense) to the World Ash for easy access but often required a trek of hundreds or thousands of miles/kilometers to reach the tree.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|94}} Once on Yggdrasil, it was said that a trip from the Prime to either Asgard or Niflheim took at least 100 days, but there was no record of any mortal ever successfully completing the journey.{{Cite dragon/90/Plane Facts on Gladsheim|37}} On the other hand, trips between Outer Planes rarely took longer than a week. In both cases, those trips were not without risks, either from the tree's inhabitants, from the risk of falling into the Astral Plane as a result of losing contact with the tree's branches, or from simply walking into the wrong destination by mistake. Falling from Yggdrasil into lower locations was rarely fatal, but could cause substantial damage as a falling creature tumbled through branches. The tree touched all layers of the [[Beastlands (plane)|Beastlands]] and [[Elysium]], except [[Belierin]], since all portals leading in and out that layer had been sealed.{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/A Player's Guide to Conflict|4}}{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|61}} The reasons why Yggdrasil connected with the Beastlands were unclear, since no Norse deities claimed realms in that plane. It was speculated that the wilderness and life-giving properties of the plane were sufficient to root the tree there. [[File:Yggdrasil_map-3e.jpg|thumb|left|350px|''A representation of Yggdrasil showing some of its connections and distances.'']] Other branches of Yggdrasil connected to the vicinity of [[Glorium]] and the realm of the [[Norns]] in the [[Outlands]]{{Cite book/A Player's Primer to the Outlands|18}}{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/Sigil and Beyond|16,40}} and to [[Winter's Hall]] in [[Pandemonium]]. The tree also extended a branch into [[Arvandor]] in the [[Arvandor (layer)|first layer]] of Arborea, near a village known as [[the Gnarl]].{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|104}} A branch also extended to [[Limbo]], connecting to a relatively stable forested island known as [[Pinwheel]].{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|23}} Relatively easy to find connections along the branches included [[Sigil]], the [[Shadowfell]], and the [[Iron Wastes]], the [[Layers of the Abyss#Layer 23: The Iron Wastes|23{{rd}} layer]] of the [[Abyss]]. In addition to those, Yggdrasil was connected to every Outer Plane, including [[Mount Celestia]], [[Mechanus]], and even the [[Styx]], but ''portals'' to those locations were few and much more difficult to find. The total number of ''portals'' was ultimately unknown, since the tree had not been thoroughly explored by any mortal.{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|12}} The exact exit point of most ''portals'' was impossible to predict, since currents from the Astral Plane often shifted the position of the branches, causing the tree to bend as if swaying under the wind. If a traveler died while on Yggdrasil, their soul was claimed by [[valkyrie]]s. In such cases, ''[[Resurrection (spell)|resurrection]]'' magic only worked if granted by a Norse [[deity]]. ==Inhabitants== The entry point into Niflheim was guarded by [[Nidhogg]], a creature that was sometimes described as a gargantuan, very ancient [[red dragon]],{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|106}} and other times as a serpent.{{Cite book/For Duty & Deity|63-64}}{{Cite book/Champions of Ruin|142}}{{Cite book/Volo's Guide to All Things Magical|121}} The World Ash and the dragon were perpetually in conflict as Nidhogg tried to sever the inter-planar link to Ysgard by chewing through the roots in order to feed her countless children. Yggdrasil responded by putting down new roots as fast as the dragon could eat them. All this took place in sight of the feast hall of [[Hel]], Norse goddess and guardian of the dead.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|105}}{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Malevolentiae|45}} The dragon usually ignored travelers coming up and down the roots, but fiercely defended herself and her offspring if disturbed. [[Viper tree]]s and [[linnorm]]s were said to be the bastard offspring of Nidhogg. Both infested some of the thinner and lower branches of the tree. Viper trees were also commonly found in [[Azzagrat]], but some specimens were brought to [[Thay]] by [[Red Wizard]]s. [[File:Ratatosk-3e.jpg|thumb|250px|''A ratatosk inhabitant of Yggdrasil.'' ]] Some of the most important inhabitants of Yggdrasil were the [[ratatosk]]s, humanoid-looking giant flying squirrels who worked as messengers or guides between the planes touched by the tree. In order to hire them for any service, a bribe in the form of pods from Yggdrasil itself was typically acceptable.{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/Monstrous Supplement|22-23}} The ratatosk frequently delivered threats from the dragons in Niflheim to other inhabitants of the tree, which included giant [[stag]]s that grazed on the leaves and [[giant eagle]]s that nested on the branches. The branches of Yggdrasil were also inhabited by numerous tree-dwelling creatures, such as [[abrian]]s, birds of prey, [[darkweaver]]s, [[giant raven]]s, and [[spider]]s. The bark was inhabited by enormous [[beetle]]s and the leaves fed entire herds of [[boar]]. In addition, bandits and [[fiend]]s commonly preyed on unwary travelers. Some of the most important junctures were patrolled by [[per]]s, but they lacked sufficient numbers to monitor the entire tree.{{Cite book/Monstrous Compendium Planescape Appendix|84-85}} [[Angel]]s guarded the ''portals'' located in some of the upper branches and [[yugoloth]]s guarded some of the ones in lower branches. A few [[hag]]s were known to inhabit cottages along the lower branches. The most frequently encountered travelers along Yggdrasil included [[bariaur]]s, [[Ysgardian dwarves]] and [[elves]], [[Fire giant|fire]] and [[frost giant]]s, [[giant owl]]s, valkyries, and [[winter wolf|winter wolves]]. ==History== A branch of Yggdrasil was a preferred trajectory of the [[Great Modron March]] as it moved from Ysgard to Limbo.{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|62}} ==Rumors & Legends== The [[Athar (faction)|Athar]] maintained that the Norse pantheon drew its power from Yggdrasil itself. Legends also claimed that the day when Nidhogg finally managed to completely destroy the tree's roots would bring about the end of Yggdrasil and of the Norse pantheon. The Ratatosk considered Yggdrasil itself to be their patron [[deity]]{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|107}} and viewed the tree as a feminine entity. ==Appendix== ===See Also=== * [[Yggdrasil's Child]], a tree from the island of [[Ruathym]] that was said to have grown from a fertile seed of Yggdrasil. Although it did not function as a portal as of the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]], the tree possessed certain powers. * [[Yggdrasil's Child (Garden)]], a [[wildspace]]-born tree that grew throughout the entire planet [[Garden]] and held it together.{{Cite book/Realmspace|44-45}} ===Appearances=== :;Adventures ::''[[The Great Modron March]]'' • ''[[Dead Gods]]'' • ''[[Expedition to the Demonweb [[Nidavellir]] | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = | refs-GW = {{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|73}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|75}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|78-82}} | type-WA = | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = | type-WT = | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = | inhabitants = yes | deities = yes | locations = yes | organizations = yes | settlements = yes | usethe = | useon = }}The '''Heroic Domains of Ysgard''',{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|58}} also referred to as '''Gladsheim''',{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|140}} was the [[Great Wheel]] plane straddling the alignments of [[chaotic good]] and [[chaotic neutral]]. Like the Greek influence on [[Arborea]], much of this plane was heavily dominated by the gods of the [[Norse pantheon]] who had little interaction with the people of [[Toril]]. The primary exception was [[Tyr]], the Norse god of war and law who became known and widely worshiped as the God of Justice in the [[Forgotten Realms]].{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|15-16}} Some characteristics of this plane were ascribed to the [[World Tree cosmology]] planes of [[Arvandor]],{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|143}} [[Brightwater]],{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|146}} [[Gates of the Moon]],{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|154}} and [[Jotunheim]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|160}} when that cosmology model became popular. When the [[Spellplague]] hit the cosmos, Brightwater merged with the Gates of the Moon which survived,{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|63}} along with Arvandor.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|62}} Jotunheim was cast into the [[Elemental Chaos]] but only parts of it survived{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|67}} as described by the [[World Axis cosmology]] model. {{Quote |It is a ''perfect'' day to die — just like yesterday, and the day before... |Hrafnul the Bold, Ysgardian [[petitioner]].{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|102}} }} ==Description== The three layers of Gladsheim consisted of tremendous rivers of earth and stone that formed cosmic arches through the void, like very tightly packed asteroid belts. Millions of miles/kilometers wide, each river was made up of gigantic chunks of matter that bumped and ground against each other at a glacial but noticeable pace, raising up mountains and opening vast chasms. These "earthbergs" all shared the same gravity field and most were inhabitable on the top side while the underside of the rivers burned with a radiant fire that provided a ruddy light to the rivers below. Earthquakes and landslides were a commonly occurring danger in Gladsheim as the landscape slowly buckled and broke under the influence of chaos. Multiple rough-hewn landings of the [[Infinite Staircase]] connected to each of Gladsheim's three layers. ===Ysgard=== {{/Imagemap}} {{Main|Ysgard (layer)}} The name of this layer was also the name of the confederation of godly domains known as [[Asgard]], home of the Norse pantheon, or Ysgard in the Norse tongue. Each realm was the size of a Prime plane empire and they were drawn together by the proximity of [[Yggdrasil]] the World Ash. Like [[Mount Olympus]], Yggdrasil was a multiplanar conduit connecting Gladsheim directly to [[Hades#Niflheim|Niflheim]] in [[Hades]] and Alternate [[Prime Material Plane]]s without passing through the [[Astral Plane]], much like the [[World Tree]] in the [[World Tree cosmology]].{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|140}} The usual ''color pools'' connecting Asgard to the Astral Plane existed but were little used. Portals in the guise of wells connected this layer to the neighboring planes of [[Arborea]], [[Limbo]], and [[Concordant Opposition]]. In addition to Yggdrasil, the Norse gods controlled and carefully guarded a portal directly to the Prime plane where they were the strongest, called the Bifrost or the rainbow bridge. Other known realms adjacent to Asgard were [[Vanaheim]] (home of the [[vanir]]), [[Alfheim]] (fairyland, known for its chaotic elven spirits), and Jotenheim (home of the giants). ===Muspelheim=== {{Main|Muspelheim}} The earthbergs of this layer were reversed (or alternatively, gravity was reversed) so the flaming side was up and the earthen side down. [[Surtur]] and the [[fire giant]]s made their home here and guarded the barriers that lead to Asgard and its neighboring realms. ===Nidavellir=== {{Main|Nidavellir}} The rivers of earth were in such close proximity in this layer that the entire sky was filled with fire, making it appear to travelers that they were in underground caverns and passages with a river of fire for a ceiling.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|94-95}} ==Inhabitants== [[Hollyphant]]s and [[planetar]]s were fairly plentiful in Gladsheim but many of the other [[Upper plane]] regulars avoided it. Wildlife included [[bear]]s, wild [[boar]]s, [[stag]]s and other woodland creatures, all bigger and tougher than their Prime plane counterparts. [[Giant]]s of all kinds lived mostly in Jotunheim but could be encountered just about anywhere. The giants of Gladsheim were generally more intelligent and better equipped (with giant-sized magic weapons) than those found on the [[Prime Material Plane]]. Some were accomplished [[cleric]]s and [[mage]]s, and [[illusionist]]s who could even fool the gods.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|96}} In addition, some [[deva]]s and [[celestial eladrin]] made their homes on this plane. ==Realms== [[File:Gladsheim - Tyr's realm.jpg|thumb|250px|right|''Tyr's realm in [[Asgard]] on the first layer of Ysgard.'']] * [[Aerdrie Faenya]], [[Seldarine]] Goddess of Air and Weather, had no permanent realm here but wandered among the layers of Gladsheim, where she often stopped at [[Alfheim]], and [[Arborea]] accompanied by dozens of huge birds.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|94,95}}{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|113}}{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|94}} * [[Anhur]], [[Mulhorandi pantheon|Mulhorandi]] God of War, Thunder, Rain, and Storms, kept his realm called [[Netaph]] on the [[Ysgard (layer)|first layer]].{{Cite book/Powers and Pantheons|95}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|86-87}} * [[Annam All-Father]], chief deity and creator of the [[giant]] races, once had a palace called [[Gudheim]] on this plane.{{Cite book/Giantcraft|44,47}} * [[Bast]],{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|50}} the [[Mulhorandi]] patron of cats and goddess of hedonistic pleasure, had her realm [[Merratet]] across the sea from Asgard in a vine-covered acropolis on the edge of a desert.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|97}}{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|51}} Bast later absorbed the essence of a minor elven goddess, became known as [[Sharess]],{{Cite web enhancement/Deities|10}} and moved to [[Brightwater]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|258}} * [[Eilistraee]], the Dark Maiden, had a realm named [[Svartalfheim]] on the Nidavellir level of this plane.{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|13}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|173}} * [[Hlal]], the [[Draconic pantheon|draconic]] Jester, had a lair know as [[Brassberg]] on Nidavellir.{{Cite book/Cult of the Dragon|120}} * [[Marthammor Duin]], the Finder-of-Trails of the [[Morndinsamman|dwarves]], resided in his [[Cavern of Rest]] on Nidavellir.{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|74}} * The ''[[Seelie Court]]'' of the [[Fey|Faerie]] Queen [[Titania]], including [[Oberon]], [[Caoimhin]], [[Damh]], [[Eachthighern]], [[Emmantiensien]], [[Fionnghuala]], [[Nathair Sgiathach]], [[Sqeulaiche]] and [[Verenestra]], often frequented Ysgard as part of its wanderings.{{Cite book/Monster Mythology|119}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|137, 175}} * [[Selûne]]'s realm, the [[Gates of the Moon]], was considered to reside in Gladsheim according to the Great Wheel cosmology.{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|13}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|29}} * [[Sharindlar]], the dwarven Lady of Life and Mercy, held her [[Merciful Court]] in Nidavellir.{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|82}} * [[Shaundakul]], the Rider of the Winds, maintained a realm called [[Shaunidaur]] on the layer of Ysgard.{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|142}} * [[Soma]], the god of moonlight, plants and prophesy in the [[Vedic]] (Indian) pantheon shared Selûne's realm.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|170}} * [[Stronmaus]], the giant god of [[the sun|sun]] and sky, resided in a [[cloud palace]] near Gudheim, when he did not stay in the [[Beastlands (plane)|Beastlands]]. * [[Surtur]], king of the [[fire giant]]s, had [[Muspelheim (realm)|a vast realm]] in [[Muspelheim]] with outposts in [[Jotunheim]].{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|121}} * [[Tarsellis Meunniduin]], [[Seldarine|elven god]] of mountains and [[snow elf]]s, had his realm named the [[Wild Ride]] or the Wild Hunt on the first layer.{{Cite dragon/236/The Seldarine Revisited}}"The Seldarine Revisited" calls Tarsellis Meunniduin's realm "The Wild Hunt" in the stats block and "The Wild Ride" in the text. * [[Thrym]], king of the [[frost giant]]s, had his frozen realm in Jotunheim.{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|123}} * [[Tyr]] Grimjaws, the Even-Handed, once made his home in [[Valhalla]], a realm in [[Asgard]]. However, Tyr was also known to reside in the [[Seven Heavens]].{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|15}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|35}} * [[Uthgar]], the Battle Father, maintained his realm of [[Uthgardtheim]] on the first layer.{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|66}} * [[Valkur]] the Mighty had his maritime realm, [[Safe Harbor]], on the first layer.{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|66}} ==History== In the [[1357 DR|Year of the Prince, 1357 DR]], [[Pasha]] [[Abon Duum]] used the power of the [[Catlord (old)|Catlord]] to travel to Tyr's realm in Gladsheim to confront Tyr with the [[Claw of Malar]], apparently seeking to seize the power of the gods. However, "Tyr" was revealed to be [[Conner]] in a cloak, having faked his death and been spirited to Gladsheim. The Catlord stole the Claw of Malar and passed it to Conner, before the real Tyr appeared and took the [[artifact]]. With a warning that he would keep an eye on Conner and the scales of justice, he sent the heroes home while Duum was left to face Justice himself.{{Cite comic/The Last Betrayal|10-14}} ==Appendix== ===Notes=== {{Notes}} ===Appearances=== :;Adventures ::''[[The Great Modron March]]'' • ''[[For Duty & Deity]]'' :;Comics ::''[[The Last Betrayal]]'' ===Gallery=== Gladsheim Imagine 30.png|A map showcasing Ysgard's structure ===References=== {{Refs|2}} ===Connections=== {{Ysgard}} {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Outer Planes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Planes of chaos]] [[Category:Locations on Yggdrasil]]

It was released as part of the [[Blood Wars basic set|basic set]], and had a rarity of "common". The artwork was by [[Rob Lazzaretti]].

[[File:Ysgard.webp|thumb|400x400px]] '''Ysgard''' was one of the [[Outer Planes]], located between [[Arborea]] and [[Limbo]]. It was of chaotic neutral alignment.
== Geography ==
Ysgard was made up of rivers of floating chunks of earth. It had three layers.

The '''Zactars''' are a [[faction]] similar to the [[Sign of One]]'s fringe belief in the [[One]]. However, they reverse cause and effect: the One imagines the multiverse into being, while in the Zactars' case, the multiverse exists for the sole purpose of the eventual arrival of the [[One True Being]].
== History ==
Initially known as the Waiting Ones, the faction rose to great prominence under Factol [[Zactar]], an obsessed charismatic man (perhaps a [[cambion]] marquis) born of a human woman and tanar'ri man. His influence was so great that he renamed the faction after himself.
Part of the philosophy that he brought with him to the faction was that the One True Being would, of course, be a female counterpart to himself, because only he would be fit to mate with the One True Being. Therefore she would be born of a human man and a tanar'ri woman -- an [[alu-fiend]].
Around [[27 YFHR]], Zactar vanished one day, and without a charismatic leader, the faction began to fall apart. Rival factions ridiculed their beliefs, and many Waiting Ones just grew tired of waiting. Surviving faction members retreated to the Cathedral as a haven against their rivals, but then they all vanished in a single night.
The [[Fated]] eventually purchased the Cathedral, but under Sigil's laws, should the Zactars ever return, then the Fated's claim on the Cathedral is rendered null.
In [[127 YFHR]], an alu-fiend named [[Umbra]] came to Sigil, with a birthmark on her palm in the shape of the symbol of the Zactars.
== Philosophy ==
Everything in the multiverse is merely filling space until the arrival of the [[One True Being]]. The faction headquarters, the [[Zactar Cathedral]], was built to welcome this being to their rightful place.
